newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly up in slow trading on Monday on short-covering from retail investors triggered by last Friday's gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active Febuary 1997 contract ended at 19,250 yuan ($2,319) per tonne, rising 170 yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 19,140 and hit a high of 19,320.
November rose 80 to 18,980, December 80 to 19,110, January 150 to 19,220, March 170 to 19,240, April 150 to 19,230 and May unchanged at 19,200.
Combined volume fell to 31,670 tonnes from 39,540.
Copper opened up due to last Friday's gains on the LME and rose further steadily for most of the session with some investors liquidating their positions due to the uncertain short-term market trend.
"Short-covering was mainly from retail investors, who prefer to wait for things to become clearer," one trader said.

"Falls in LME stockpiles have supported Shanghai copper at the 19,000 yuan level over the past few weeks," a second trader said. "But further stockpile reductions seem unlikely so Shanghai copper will lose its most important support."
Analysts expect copper to drop further if it breaches the 19,000 yuan level in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. November fell 50 to 13,450 yuan per tonne, December did not trade and January dropped 60 to 13,150.
Combined volume fell to 470 tonnes from 610.
